Born in Illinois about 1860 to 61: the 1870 and 1880 censuses at Barclay both give his birthplace as Illinois,
settling a family tree's Barclay. He was the son of Frank Fritz and Catharine Schmidt,
a founding family of Saint Francis parish at Barclay, Black Hawk County, in 1862.
He married Mary Ann Staebell, a Freeport-born daughter of Alsatian parents, at Saint Francis,
Barclay, on 17 January 1882, in a double wedding with her sister Caroline, and their daughter Elizabeth was born in
Barclay Township in 1884. He told the 1915 state census that he had married in 1882 and come to South Dakota in 1893;
a 1903 county atlas shows J. L. Fritz with land in Wellington Township, Minnehaha County.
The 1900 and 1910 censuses find them in Wellington Township with a houseful of children;
they raised twelve. His mother, Catharine, died at Parker in 1923.
The family later moved to Parker, and he died on 15 March 1938, in Minnehaha County.
Born at Freeport, Illinois, 9 December 1860, daughter of Frank Staebell, from Stundwiller in Alsace,
and Margaretha Phillips. She grew up from the age of two on the family farm in Barclay Township,
Black Hawk County, Iowa. On 17 January 1882 she married John L. Fritz, son of Frank Fritz,
at Saint Francis Church, Barclay, in a double wedding with her sister Caroline and George Schlecht;
their brother Joseph was best man. Their daughter Elizabeth was born at Barclay in 1884.
The family went west to South Dakota, where two of her brothers also settled around Parker,
Turner County, Joseph as a real-estate dealer and Edward as a farmer, and the Fritzes made their home at Parker too.
She died at Parker on 8 February 1935, aged 74, and is buried at Saint Christina.
